items.evidence: Two independent dead causes, all javap-verified fresh against the 1.21.10 jar. (1) Dead tag: speleothem_tag() reads #minecraft:speleothems (speleothem.rs:13), absent from 1.21.10 data (no tag file in the client jar, no BlockTags.SPELEOTHEMS field, no key in prepared block-tags.json, 203 keys), so speleothem_with / speleothem_is_tip / is_free_hanging_stalactite are always false and falling.rs:51 spawn_falling_stalactite is tag-gated; the thickness calc is tag-gated the same way (shapes.rs:1176 speleothem_thickness, place.rs:1398 speleothem_thickness_for, is_with closure at shapes.rs:1186), so thickness is always "tip". (2) Missing link: prepared fields for pointed_dripstone is {} (no blockToGrowOn), so data.link is None and speleothem_grow's can_grow is always false; vanilla 1.21.10 PDB.canGrow hardcodes Blocks.DRIPSTONE_BLOCK + water source at above(2). Vanilla PDB bytecode has ZERO BlockTags references - all predicates are same-block. Observable: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, thickness, falling stalactite spawn all dead. NOT dead (dispatch FIXED vs 26.x): all five dispatch sites now arm on Class::Speleothem | Class::PointedDripstone (place.rs:1156, shapes.rs:745, survive.rs:326, tick.rs:257, tick.rs:443), and is_valid_speleothem_placement (survive.rs:600) is not tag-gated, so placement direction, updateShape survival scheduling, canSurvive and scheduled-tick destroy WORK; fallOn stalagmite damage and trident break (name/data-keyed) also work. The dead-code constants in speleothem.rs match vanilla exactly (growth 0.011377778, transfer 0.17578125/0.05859375, findTip max 11) but were not counted as passes. Reproduces pilot G6 + B11-G06 and 26.1.2 B1-G01, in narrower form than 26.1.2's whole-system framing.
items.title: Pointed-dripstone system half dead: transfer, growth, cauldron fill, thickness, falling stalactites (no #speleothems tag, no blockToGrowOn link; dispatch fixed)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 FallingBlockEntity.tick runs the landing branch at the first water cell (onGround || inWater, where inWater = concrete powder && fluid is WATER tag, with a fast-fall clip check when the delta's length-squared exceeds 1.0, using ClipContext.Block.COLLIDER + ClipContext.Fluid.SOURCE_ONLY); the port's game/falling_blocks.rs fall_step has no concrete-powder water check at all (comment at line 120: "a falling block never runs baseTick, so it is never in water") and game/falling_damage.rs finish_falling_block always passes stuck_in_water=false (line 128-133), so powder sinks to the lakebed. The horizon-world landing branch itself (level/falling.rs falling_block_landed) matches vanilla, including the onLand replaced-state check - the fix is local to the client fall step. Carries over from pilot G2. Same defect as 26.2's B1-G02, 26.1's B1-G02, 26.1.1's B1-G02 and 26.1.2's B1-G02.
items.title: Concrete powder falling into water does not solidify on contact

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 AbstractThrownPotion.onHitBlock gates on PotionContents.is(Potions.WATER) - Holder equality, NOT a tag (re-verified fresh; zero douses_fire / PotionTags references in the class). The port's game/splash_water.rs ships the 26.3 tag form: potion_in_tag(stack, "minecraft:douses_fire" / "hurts_water_sensitive_entities" / "extinguishes_entities" / "rehydrates_axolotls"), read from trades.potion_tags built from the prepared data's tags/potion directory. That directory is EMPTY for 1.21.10 - zero potion tag files in the client jar (26.1.2 at least had tradeable.json) - so all four gates are always closed and no splash water ever dowses fire, hurts water-sensitive entities, extinguishes burning entities, or rehydrates axolotls. 26.2's file uses is_water_potion (Potions.WATER equality) and works. The downstream code matches vanilla exactly (dowse targets, dowseFire, the (4,2,4) box, dist^2<16, hurt 1.0 indirectMagic, axolotl +1800 air capped) but is unreachable. Reproduces B11-G13 and 26.1.2 B1-G03.
items.title: Splash water never douses fire / hurts / extinguishes / rehydrates (potion tags are 26.3-only; 1.21.10 has zero potion tag files)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 has NO EntityFluidInteraction class at all - the classic 1.21.x form: Entity.updateFluidHeightAndDoFluidPushing(TagKey, double) with top = y + PLAIN FluidState.getHeight, and updateFluidOnEyes as a separate single-cell check with the plain top (plus a boat override). The port's horizon-world/src/entity_fluid.rs ships the 26.3 form (per-kind trackers + separate CurrentAccumulators, update returns Result<bool>) and its eye check (entity_fluid.rs:389-401) computes the top with world.camera_height(state, p) (camera_height_at: a source fluid with a sturdy block above -> 1.0, else height_at). Observable: an entity whose eye is in (0.889, 1.0] above a source's block bottom with a solid ceiling -> the port says eyes-in-fluid, vanilla 1.21.10 says not; affects was_eye_in_water / is_under_water (swimming, overlay, air/drowning). The rest of the 26.3 form was verified behaviourally equivalent for vanilla fluids (flow scaling by running max height < 0.4, apply_to with no 1e-5 floor, fluid_height/is_in_fluid/is_eye_in_fluid, tracker pruning; the boat interaction-box clip is a nuance, not a gap - vanilla short-circuits the water update for boat passengers instead and the clip gives the same answer for water). Reproduces 26.1.2 B1-G04.
items.title: Entity fluid interaction eye check uses camera height instead of the plain fluid top

items.evidence: RE-CHECKED FIRST. Vanilla 1.21.10 FlowingFluid.canHoldAnyFluid is hardcoded (javap-verified fresh, FlowingFluid.txt:1012-1075): LiquidBlockContainer -> true; blocksMotion -> false; excludes DoorBlock, #signs, ladder, sugar cane, bubble column, nether/end portals, end gateway, structure void; else true (air passes). Zero 'washed' references in FlowingFluid; washed_away_by_fluids does not exist in 1.21.10 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form (level/fluids.rs:359-361: is_liquid_container(state) || in_set(state, tags.washed_away_by_fluids)), and Tags::resolve fills a missing tag with an empty set (level/data.rs:396), so can_hold_any_fluid is true only for liquid containers and NO fluid spreads at all, water or lava. The spread machinery itself matches vanilla - the failure is isolated to the predicate. Reproduces pilot G5 and 26.1.2 B1-G05. NOTE: G5's status in the 1.21.7 ledger is "fixed", but the 1.21.10 tree carries the tag form again - the fix did not carry into this tree.
items.title: NO fluid spreading at all, water or lava (canHoldAnyFluid reads the absent #washed_away_by_fluids tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 LavaFluid.randomTick (javap-verified fresh): the first branch stops at the first blocksMotion() block (air + flammable neighbours -> set fire + return, else blocksMotion -> return, offset 144-150). blocks_lava_fire_spread does not exist in 1.21.10 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form (level/fluids.rs:776-785: tag("minecraft:blocks_lava_fire_spread").is_some_and(...)), and BlockFacts::tag returns None for an absent tag (level/mod.rs:941), so the walk never stops at a solid block: fire spreads through stone, and the walk keeps drawing RNG after the first motion-blocking block, perturbing the random stream vs vanilla. The rest of lava_random_tick matches vanilla exactly, including the doFireTick pair gate. Reproduces pilot G3 and 26.1.2 B1-G06.
items.title: Lava fire spread walks through solid blocks (walk stops only for the absent #blocks_lava_fire_spread tag)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 FlowingFluid.getFlow's below-check reads the per-state BlockState.blocksMotion() rule; there is no blocks_fluid_flow tag in 1.21.10 data (no tag file, no BlockTags field, no prepared key). The port ships the 26.3 tag form in both places: horizon-client-render/src/assets.rs:224-232 reads minecraft:blocks_fluid_flow from the prepared tag bundle (erroring if absent), and horizon-client/src/motion/fluids.rs:27-54 builds blocks_flow from the tag's BTreeSet<String>. fluid_flow::flow_at (horizon-world/src/fluid_flow.rs) then reads every neighbour as non-blocking, so flow vectors near solid blocks are computed as if the wall were not there - wrong push for entities, arrows, boats and mobs in water next to solids (flow_at callers: motion/fluids.rs:446, entities/fluids.rs:45,232, arrows.rs:1490, mobs/living.rs:331). Masked in practice by the Batch 3 startup blocker (MotionResources::load fails on the absent #causes_suffocation/#suppresses_bounce tags - reproduces in 1.21.10, motion.rs:142,145). Reproduces 26.1.2 B1-G07; NEW vs 26.1.
items.title: Fluid-flow vector table reads the absent #blocks_fluid_flow tag (blocks_fluid_flow := blocks_motion mapping gone)

items.evidence: Vanilla 1.21.10 FallingBlockEntity.tick ends with deltaMovement.scale(0.98d) - the DOUBLE literal (ldc2_w // double 0.98d, offset 871, re-verified fresh). The port ships the 26.2 form (horizon-client/src/entity_rules.rs:11-14: let drag = f64::from(0.98_f32) = 0.9800000190734863). Effect: after 4 ticks 0.1 x 0.98^4 = 0.092236816 vs 0.1 x 0.98F^4 = 0.09223682318... - a ~7e-9 relative drift per tick, sub-mm over a full fall. Tiny but verified-wrong against the bytecode. scale_air_drag is shared with PrimedTnt.tick (out of scope). Reproduces 26.1.2 B1-G08; NEW vs 26.1.
items.title: Falling-block air drag uses 0.98F widened instead of the double literal 0.98

items.evidence: NEW for 1.21.10. Vanilla 1.21.10 FireBlock.tick reads the #increased_fire_burnout BIOME tag (level.getBiome(pos).is(BiomeTags.INCREASED_FIRE_BURNOUT), javap-verified fresh): in the 8 tagged biomes (bamboo_jungle, mushroom_fields, mangrove_swamp, snowy_slopes, frozen_peaks, jagged_peaks, swamp, jungle) the checkBurnOut chances drop by 50 (300->250 sides, 250->200 vertical) and the spread odds are halved. The port implements the adjustment correctly (level/tick.rs:677-686: extra = -50 when burnout) but gates it on the 26.x ENVIRONMENT ATTRIBUTE: horizon-client-render/src/biome.rs:226 reads attributes["minecraft:gameplay/increased_fire_burnout"] from the biome's JSON, consumed at game.rs:1577 and tick.rs:677. No 1.21.10 biome JSON has an attributes key (verified: jungle.json has none) and 1.21.10 has no minecraft:environment_attribute registry at all, so the gate is always false: in the 8 biomes, fires burn out at the non-burnout chances and spread at full odds. Minor: confined to those 8 biomes' fire behaviour.
items.title: Fire burnout never applies in the eight burnout biomes (port reads a 26.x environment attribute, vanilla reads the #increased_fire_burnout biome tag)

out_of_scope_failures: None. Untraced sub-details (not counted as passes, not needs-harness): the lava-hurt GENERIC_BURN sound was not traced in the Rust; PointedDripstoneBlock.animateTick drip particles were not compared; dragon-egg teleport on use is out of scope (falling-block scope covers fall/landing/conversion) - though its delay (5) and tries (1000) were re-verified fresh anyway. Oracle triage: 10 of the 13 in-scope oracles fail (B1-O01..B1-O08); the other 3 pass (FluidOccupancy, FluidShape, WaterSplash) - provisional on the 26.1.2 Batch 0 table until the 1.21.10 table lands; no verdict is expected to change except possibly B1-O08's error counts (derived by inspection, not measurement). Out-of-scope observations flagged in the report (not B1 items): hooks.rs ice_destroyed_by_player reads the absent #blocks_motion tag; game/campfire_douse.rs 26.3 form (#douses_campfires absent; 1.21.10 uses ShovelItem.useOn); Assets::load missing-tag errors (render tests only); MotionResources missing motion tags (26.1 B3-G22 reproduces, Batch 3 scope); item-entity/TNT air-drag sharing the B1-G08 regression; datapack-dimension fast_lava attribute nuance; palette-reader question is Batch 11's scope.
source: 1.21.10 parity sweep, batch 1 - the 1.21.7 pilot scope re-run against vanilla 1.21.10 (checks only, no fixes). Scope: water/lava spreading and flow, fluid pushing, bubble columns, concrete powder solidification, lava fire spread + ignition + game rules, dripstone growth + cauldron fill, falling blocks, cauldron fill levels, splash water. Re-checks all six 1.21.7 pilot defects (G1-G6) and Batch 11 findings B11-G06, B11-G13 (PRIMARY), plus all 17 items from the 26.1.2 run (SECONDARY), against 1.21.10's own jar/data.
systemic_note: The 1.21.7 pilot's systemic root cause (26.x tag-based logic for tags absent in the target version's data) applies to 1.21.10 in the same FIVE places as 26.1.2: the speleothem system (B1-G01) and splash water (B1-G03) as in 26.1, PLUS can_hold_any_fluid (B1-G05), the lava-fire walk (B1-G06), and the flow-vector table (B1-G07). A fourth regression is numeric: the falling-block air drag (B1-G08: 0.98F widened instead of the double literal). B1-G04 is the same pattern at a smaller scale (26.3-form entity fluid interaction, camera-height eye check), and B1-G09 is the same pattern in a new place (a 26.x environment attribute read where 1.21.10 has a biome tag). What is DIFFERENT about 1.21.10 is that this tree genuinely fixed two of the pattern's instances: the bubble-column code was rewritten to vanilla 1.21.10's hardcoded form (B1-G10, G1 FIXED) and the fire-rule code honours the 1.21.x doFireTick pair (B1-G11, G4 FIXED), and the dripstone dispatch was adapted so five behaviours work (B1-G01 narrower). The pattern is therefore not 'the tree ships 26.3 everywhere' but 'the tree ships 26.3 exactly where the port did not adapt' - the remaining five tag reads + one attribute read are the unadapted residue. Where 1.21.10's data HAS the tag (#signs, #fire, #anvil, infiniburn, #soul_fire_base_blocks, #shovels), the port reads it; where 1.21.10 still lacks the tag, the port usually carries the hardcoded 1.21.7-style list form - except in the six places above, where it ships the 26.3 form.
